propositions: The mcp compose service has no mechanism to provision or mount a ticket store, causing all tracker reads to return empty results or 'ticket_not_found' errors.
The Dockerfile.mcp lacks an entrypoint script to clone the tickets branch, and the .dockerignore excludes .tickets-tracker, preventing the store from being baked into the image or mounted at runtime.
The docker-compose.yml mcp service declares only secret volumes but no tracker directory mount or REBAR_TRACKER_DIR environment variable, unlike the review-bot which has both.
The ticket store must be provisioned via dedicated volume and entrypoint that clones the shared tickets branch with credentials from MCP_TICKETS_PAT, mirroring the review-bot pattern.

The test suite does not assert store provisioning, allowing the gap to ship silently, and the ADR does not document the design decisions around full read-write access, dedicated volume isolation, and credential fallback behavior.
